answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the zephyr measurement is attested to the lantern verifier, the saffron audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 7 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
